The *Sabhiyattheragāthā* (Thag 4.3) is a short poem of the *Theragāthā* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, representing the verses attributed to the elder Sabhiya [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, the text is represented across nine translations in eight modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Verses from the *Sabhiyattheragāthā* exhibit widespread parallels and reuse across both Pali and non-Pali canonical traditions. SuttaCentral identifies curated parallels to individual stanzas in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 6 and Dhp 312), the *Tāyanasutta* of the *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2.8), the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), the *Kosambiyajātaka* (Ja 428), the *Kosambakakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya (Kd 10), and the verses of Mahākaccāyana (Thag 8.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal text reuse with the *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2, specifically matching §2.4–3.4 with §8.5.4–8.6.4), as well as extensive commentary and quotation throughout the second volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

Beyond Pali literature, parallels and text alignments are found extensively across early Buddhist verse anthologies and Vinaya literature. SuttaCentral documents parallels in the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 239–260), Gāndhārī Dharmapada collections (G-Dhp 243–258 and G3-Dhp 21–30), the Gilgit Mūlasarvāstivādivinaya, Tibetan canonical translations of the *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 11, 14, and 22), Sanskrit *Udānavarga* traditions (UV 11, 14, and 22), and various Chinese collections including the *Faju jing* (T 210), *Chu yao jing* (T 212), and *Faji yao song jing* (T 213) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently aligns segments of the text with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
